He was a named petitioner, together with the National Association of Judicial Auctioneers, in the administrative control proceeding discussed in Part V, and drafted the legal opinion that supported it. The members of the organizations he presides over benefit from the rule under discussion. The account of the proceeding rests on published decisions rather than on the author's recollection.

detail.abstract:
This article examines whether a binary classification of state authority over internet
auctions adequately describes the regulatory architecture governing who may
conduct, supervise and answer for an online auction in the United States.
Using licensing data compiled by the National Auctioneer License Law Officials
Association, the study first maps twenty-four state jurisdictions according to their
reported authority over internet auctions, financial safeguards, reciprocity
arrangements, and individual and firm licensing requirements. It then tests that
classification against primary law in five contrasting jurisdictions: Florida,
Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Kentucky and Virginia.
The comparison identifies materially different mechanisms of personal
attribution concealed within similar affirmative or negative classifications.
These include dual licensing with a statutory limit on corporate delegation,
a designated auctioneer-of-record, a board-approved designated person, a
technologically neutral statutory definition of auction, and a definition
anchored in the physical concept of an audience. Judicial and administrative
sources confirm that these mechanisms carry practical consequence: in one
jurisdiction an unlicensed firm was barred from enforcing its own bidder
agreement; in another, the statute conditions any suit for compensation on
prior proof of licensure.
The findings suggest that digitalization does not itself determine whether personal
attribution is preserved or diluted. Regulatory architecture does, and that
architecture comprises statutory design, licensing scope, exemptions and
administrative interpretation together. Two jurisdictions share materially similar
audience-based definitions and are nonetheless recorded differently as to internet-
auction authority, which indicates that definitional language alone does not settle the
question. The article does not rank the competing models or advocate regulatory
uniformity. It argues that comparative analysis of internet-auction regulation requires
attention not merely to whether a state claims regulatory authority, but to how that
authority identifies the person or entity responsible for the conduct of the sale

title: Endogenous Arrivals in Expert-Review Systems: Generative AI and the Peer-Review Bottleneck
affiliations: Kyung Hee University - Department of Applied Mathematics  and Sungshin Women's University

detail.title: Endogenous Arrivals in Expert-Review Systems: Generative AI and the Peer-Review Bottleneck
detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence expands the upstream capacity to create research manuscripts, whereas expert verification remains a scarce downstream service. We develop a stochastic service model in which the input to review is generated structurally rather than imposed as an exogenous arrival rate. Independent projects mature stochastically, and optimal abandonment and submission decisions transform Poisson project starts into a Poisson submission stream through displacement and thinning; its intensity is an explicit function of research technology and anticipated review congestion. This endogenous input can be coupled to a general class of stationary service systems through their inverse mean-occupancy maps. The resulting equilibrium is unique and globally stable, and the coupling yields a service-system-independent Red Queen attenuation factor that measures how much of an upstream productivity gain survives as processed throughput. When author-side AI also displaces reviewer effort, processed throughput can decline, and systemwide congestion can reverse the private effect of AI on submission thresholds. We give a delay-consistent microfoundation for the congestion wedge, show how capacity expansion can induce additional submissions, extend the model to heterogeneous projects, and study capacity, verification, and linked review-credit design. Numerical experiments and public conference-scale statistics illustrate the bottleneck mechanism and its robustness to finite-server architectures and service-time variability.

title: Knowledge Management and Organizational Resilience in Crisis: A Systematic Review of Capacities, Mechanisms, and Consequences
affiliations: Islamic Revolution University, Imam Hossein University and Imam Hossein University

detail.title: Knowledge Management and Organizational Resilience in Crisis: A Systematic Review of Capacities, Mechanisms, and Consequences
detail.abstract: Recent crises have demonstrated that organizational resilience depends not only on resources, technologies, and formal structures but also on organizations' capacity to mobilize knowledge under conditions of uncertainty and time pressure. This systematic review synthesizes fragmented evidence on how knowledge management (KM) contributes to organizational resilience across crisis stages and outcomes. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, peer-reviewed studies indexed up to December 31, 2025, were systematically identified, screened, and appraised, resulting in 52 eligible studies. Thematic synthesis identified five interdependent KM capacities: strategic and environmental awareness; absorptive and reconfigurative learning, including unlearning; social capital and relational coordination; organizational memory and institutional continuity; and adaptive responses and innovation. Four mechanisms explain how these capacities foster resilience: reducing ambiguity and accelerating decision-making, enabling collective action and resource mobilization, institutionalizing experience through recursive learning, and facilitating improvisation and innovation. The contribution of KM varies across resilience outcomes and crisis stages. Strategic awareness and organizational memory are particularly important for recovery, learning, and relational capacities that support adaptation, while unlearning and innovation become critical for transformation. The evidence also reveals non-linear effects: knowledge accumulation may generate inertia and rigidity, while uncertainty, transition costs, trust, organizational structure, and digital infrastructure condition KM effectiveness. Building on these findings, this review develops a processual and recursive framework that conceptualizes KM as an evolutionary meta-capability for configuring complementary knowledge capacities across crisis cycles. This perspective extends resilience research beyond static resource-based explanations and provides a foundation for the longitudinal and comparative testing of KM mechanisms and boundary conditions.

title:
From Guaranteed Allocation to Deferred Float: 
A Contract-level Census and Event Evidence on Cornerstone Unlocks in Hong Kong IPOs, 2018-2026

detail.title:
From Guaranteed Allocation to Deferred Float: 
A Contract-level Census and Event Evidence on Cornerstone Unlocks in Hong Kong IPOs, 2018-2026
detail.abstract: Cornerstone investors in Hong Kong initial public offerings receive guaranteed allocations in exchange for a disclosed six-month lock-up, so each tranche converts a known share quantity into a contractually dated expansion of tradable supply. This paper constructs and audits the complete population of these contracts — 930 Main Board operating IPOs from January 2018 through August 2026, of which 583 (62.7%) carry cornerstone tranches mapping into 596 dated release events — and measures unlock outcomes on 231 fully audited events of the 2022–2026 cohorts, net of a systematic screen for voluntary lock-up extensions. A pre-outcome estimation gate, built on reconciling public float to immediately tradable float through allotment results, over-allotment exercises, and corporate actions, identifies 504 clean occurred events. First, deferred-supply intensity has risen: the annual median release ratio — newly eligible cornerstone shares over immediately tradable pre-release float — roughly doubled, from about 0.25 in 2018–2019 to 0.52–0.60 in 2024–2026 (trend p < 10⁻¹⁰); both margins moved materially, with the numerator — cornerstone books relative to offer size — showing the larger change. Second, release days sharply amplify trading activity — mean volume over pre-release float roughly quadruples (p < 10⁻⁵) — and roughly double the probability of extreme daily moves. Third, prices show a small negative release-day displacement relative to each stock’s own pre-release drift (−0.58 percentage points, at the 5% significance boundary); equivalence within ±1 percentage point cannot be established, and the surrounding declines begin weeks before eligibility, consistent with young-listing drift and/or anticipatory pricing.

title:
Bounded Rationality in Twenty-First-Century Society
A Sociological and Philosophical Inquiry with Scenarios for the Twenty-Second Century
affiliations: University of Chile - Industrial Engineering

detail.title:
Bounded Rationality in Twenty-First-Century Society
A Sociological and Philosophical Inquiry with Scenarios for the Twenty-Second Century
detail.abstract: Human rationality has always been bounded. No individual knows every alternative, calculates every consequence, or possesses enough time, memory, and attention to choose optimally. Yet twenty-first-century society has qualitatively changed what that limitation means. Information abundance, social acceleration, technological interdependence, and the growing mediation of algorithms have turned attention, trust, and the capacity to form judgments into resources contested by corporations, states, platforms, and artificial intelligence systems. Vulnerability now consists not only in remaining unaware of relevant facts, but also in receiving a reality already selected, ranked, synthesized, and, increasingly, interpreted by machines. The central thesis is that the principal risk is not that machines may eventually think, but that human beings and their institutions may progressively delegate what merits attention and thought, which ends ought to be pursued, and who is answerable for decisions. Four scenarios are developed for the twenty-second century: civic symbiosis, algorithmic tutelage, cognitive oligarchy, and epistemic archipelagos. The most plausible future will be an unequal combination of all four. Avoiding their adverse consequences requires cognitive constitutionalism, epistemically resilient institutions, education for autonomy, technological design oriented toward human agency, economic competition, an equitable distribution of AI capabilities, and international cooperation. The decisive question will not be how much artificial intelligence humanity possesses, but whether it retains the capacity to set ends, give reasons, revise its beliefs, and assume responsibility to others.

title: A GDP-weighted Multi-signal System for Real-Time Recession Detection

detail.title: A GDP-weighted Multi-signal System for Real-Time Recession Detection
detail.abstract:
We build and pre-register a three-signal recession detection system from public administrative data: weekly state-level unemployment insurance claims, GDP-weighted so that the cross-section answers how much of the economy is located in deteriorating states, with a sequential confirmation rule coupling the national and propagation signals and an industry layer that diagnoses where each recession began. The paper is simultaneously a capability study and an honest re-test: the system descends from a pinned manuscript claiming its default detected all eight post-1967 recessions ahead of the Sahm Rule with fewer false positives, and we re-adjudicate that claim under a pre-registered rule on a freshly frozen vintage. The verdict is REFUTE: the default detects seven of eight - the 2001 recession is undetected by a vintage-fragile confirmation-window knife edge - and the honest false-positive comparison runs 4 system episodes to 2 Sahm episodes under identical accounting. The miss is settings-bound, not architectural: 36 of 54 pre-registered pairings detect all eight, every miss anywhere in the space is 2001, and the zero-false-positive full-detection share is 13% - structural, though far below the source's claimed 76%. What the measured system delivers: a quantified earliness-cleanliness frontier (zero false positives and positive mean lead never coexist); a convergence-speed diagnostic that reads recession propagation type from the signals' timing at no added cost; epicenter identification where a broad industry origin exists - for 2007, Real estate (footprint 0.870737 across 46 declining states), corroborated across independent layers, with per-cell footprints, margins, and runner-up rows disclosed so readers can weigh the statistic's known artifact modes - and a plain statement where none does (2001); and a concrete, low-cost data-infrastructure agenda that would relax the system's binding limits. Deployment is reframed as a three-tier posture ending in the Sahm Rule as independent confirmation, and the paper closes by registering that posture as a dated, falsifiable forward claim from a live all-quiet board (Stage 1 QUIET, Stage 2 QUIET at the frozen vintage), with every load-bearing number bound to committed code and hashed data by a public machine-verified ledger.

title: The Payer-beneficiary Gap Diagnostic Underdetermination and Structural Redesign

detail.title: The Payer-beneficiary Gap Diagnostic Underdetermination and Structural Redesign

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: No humans were involved in this research.
declarations.funderStatement: The research was founded by myself.

detail.abstract: Why can two actors report the same level of support for an organizational change while their apparent agreement conceals different organizational problems? A global support score compresses judgments about when benefits will arrive, whether the promised pathway is credible, whether the actor will retain a claim, what value will reach the actor, and what costs must be borne in the meantime. This paper develops the payer-beneficiary gap as a structural and perceived configuration of those conditions. Its conceptual core is the Reach-Contribution Ledger: future reach is organized by temporal relevance, pathway credibility, claim continuity and claim-contingent incidence, with claim-independent meaning entering separately; voluntary contribution is shaped by that reach, transition burden, execution capability, action leverage and action cost. The operators in the ledger are conceptual rather than computational: multiplication marks a gate, addition marks a distinct source of value and subtraction marks a countervailing burden. The central claim is diagnostic underdetermination. Equal support scores can arise from different configurations, so a global score can support prognosis without identifying what the organization must change. The appropriate response is configuration-sensitive structural redesign rather than personalized persuasion. Program history supplies a dynamic extension because delivered, renamed, abandoned and transparently terminated programs become evidence for future credibility. The paper states eight propositions and an ethically bounded research agenda based on cognitive interviews, anonymous scenario comparisons, structural-incidence and program-history audits, and comparative program evidence. It rejects employee scoring, covert segmentation, automated intervention assignment and the extraction of additional effort without changing the underlying distribution.

title: Cornered Rational Choice: A General Theory of Rational Behavior Under Severe Constraint

detail.title: Cornered Rational Choice: A General Theory of Rational Behavior Under Severe Constraint
detail.abstract: This paper develops the Theory of Cornered Rational Choice, a microeconomic framework that extends rational-choice analysis to decision environments in which effective alternatives become severely restricted around a consequential threshold. Building on the Beckerian premise that individuals respond to incentives through utility-maximizing choices, and drawing on the Slutsky decomposition and the logic of Giffen-type responses, the framework examines conditions under which an increase in the cost, risk, or deterrence associated with an activity may increase rather than reduce engagement. The central proposition is that when a mandatory threshold becomes binding and effective substitutes are restricted, the compensated substitution effect may approach zero. Under the additional conditions specified in Proposition 1-most importantly, a sufficiently strong negative income effect or deterioration in the return to the focal activity-the resulting comparative static can become positive, yielding behavioral inversion without abandoning rational utility maximization. In this sense, the framework generalizes the structural logic underlying Giffen-type responses from conventional consumption settings to a broader class of severely constrained decision environments. The mechanism is formalized through an effective choice set, a mandatory threshold vector, a degenerate boundary condition in which the expenditure required to satisfy the threshold approaches available resources, and a Required-Outcome Return Model. These elements are integrated with the Slutsky decomposition to identify the conditions under which a conventional negative price response may be reversed. The theory is explicitly conditional. A cornered state does not by itself imply behavioral inversion, and an observed positive response to an increase in cost does not establish Cornered Rational Choice. The framework therefore distinguishes structural cornering from explanations based on preference shifts, information shocks, prospect-theoretic mechanisms, bounded rationality, and other behavioral or strategic mechanisms. Four domains-labor supply, crime and punishment, political extremism, and international relations-are presented as illustrative applications and testable hypotheses rather than empirical conclusions established by the theory. The paper concludes with institutional and policy implications centered on the Golden Bridge Principle: when behavioral escalation is generated by structural cornering, restoring credible alternatives and reducing binding thresholds may be more effective than simply increasing pressure or penalties.

title: THE 40-50-10 IPO: Regulatory Allocation Floors and Contractual Corner Solutions in Hong Kong
affiliations: and Shenzhen University of Information Technology

detail.title: THE 40-50-10 IPO: Regulatory Allocation Floors and Contractual Corner Solutions in Hong Kong
detail.abstract: Hong Kong's August 2025 IPO reform introduced a minimum 40% non-cornerstone bookbuilding allocation and a choice between a clawback-based public tranche and a no-clawback alternative. Using prospectus-level coding for all 161 operating IPOs in the first post-reform year, together with exact final allocation compositions for 146 issues, we document rapid coordination on two nested corners. Mechanism B became the de facto standard outside the specialist-technology regime: 139 of 141 non-Rule 18C offerings selected it, and every Mechanism B issuer began with the 10% minimum public tranche. Among Mechanism B offerings with cornerstone investors, 32 of 112 chose an initial 40-50-10 split across non-cornerstone bookbuilding, cornerstone, and public tranches. Its incidence rises from 10.7% in the smallest proceeds quartile to 60.7% in the largest. The evidence shows how a regulatory menu can generate a market standard and, within it, a size-related contractual corner. The design is descriptive rather than a sharp regression discontinuity.

title: When a Premium Becomes a Policy
affiliations: University of Groningen, Faculty of Law

detail.title: When a Premium Becomes a Policy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded.

detail.abstract: Payment of a life-insurance premium is performance. Once the insurer accepts the money and the contract takes effect, the payer's former asset has gone; the policyholder holds the rights created by the policy. Commercial shorthand treats this as a continuous passage from money to policy and from policy to secured credit. Legal analysis cannot assume that the same asset persists throughout the arrangement. I call each legally operative transaction a "juridical hinge" and ask what asset exists on each side of it. Payment disposes of the premium, policy issue creates a chose in action, and a later assignment reaches only the rights transferred by its terms. At the PRC-Hong Kong interface, the payment itself cannot be analysed without identifying the payer's status, the location of the funds and the remittance channel. Ownership of the policy then follows the contract and any separately established proprietary relation. An assignee's rights are defined by the instrument and governing law. A later facility gives the borrower a new account asset coupled with its own debt. A trust of the borrower's shares does not, without a separate disposition, bring either the borrower's assets or a third-party policy into the trust fund. The documents show how value moved; the legal consequences follow from the transaction and law applicable at each hinge.

title: Hope, Resilience, and Faith in Organizations and Communities: An Integrated Multi-level Framework

detail.title: Hope, Resilience, and Faith in Organizations and Communities: An Integrated Multi-level Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: non
declarations.ethicsApproval: approved
declarations.funderStatement: non

detail.abstract: Contemporary scholarship on hope, resilience, and faith often bifurcates into two distinct streams: measurement-based approaches that treat these constructs as psychological resources (e.g., Psychological Capital), and ontological approaches that theorize them as modes of existential and narrative engagement. This paper argues that neither framework is sufficient in isolation for explaining adaptive capacity in complex social systems. Measurement-based approaches offer precision but risk abstracting individuals from their structural contexts, while ontological approaches offer depth but often lack scalable applicability. We propose an integrated Multi-Level Framework, operating across Individual, Relational, and Systemic dimensions, to map how these constructs function within organizations and communities. Critically, we examine the "dark side" of these phenomena, documenting how resilience can manifest as maladaptive persistence in toxic environments and how "faith" can function as institutional compliance rather than genuine meaning-making. By synthesizing evidence from organizational behavior, community psychology, and systems theory, this analysis offers a theoretical basis for understanding how human adaptive capacity is constituted, sustained, or eroded in collective settings. This analysis also moves beyond simplistic causal claims to plausible mechanisms and correlational pathways, grounding assertions in empirical literature while acknowledging limits to generalizability.

title: Agentic AI Systems and Financial Stability: From Model Risk to Systemic Risk
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System and

detail.title: Agentic AI Systems and Financial Stability: From Model Risk to Systemic Risk
detail.abstract: Financial stability rests on the premise that distress is largely idiosyncratic and therefore diversifiable. When one institution errs, the rest of the system absorbs the shock. That premise fails when many decision-makers depend on the same infrastructure and are interconnected, so that a single fault becomes a common shock and propagates. Agentic systems are AI models that take consequential actions rather than only emitting predictions, and these agentic systems are becoming exactly such a shared substrate. When a population of agents is built on a common foundation model and their actions interact, the binding concern is no longer the model risk of any single deployment but the systemic risk of the population. This monograph develops that systemic-risk account in six mathematical settings. We start from single-institution model-risk management, the microprudential discipline of validating and governing one firm’s reliance on a model, and build toward a macroprudential theory of agentic financial stability. Chapter 1 establishes the microprudential unit. The chapter recasts the credit-risk decomposition of expected loss into a probability of default, a loss given default, and an exposure at default as an expected-harm identity that multiplies a probability of harmful action, a severity given harm, and a blast radius for a single agent. The chapter also introduces a set-valued containment-risk measure whose value is the set of acceptable mitigation configurations, and it proves that against irreversible harm, detection and reversibility do not merely cost more; they cannot work — under the lever-assignment axiom (A3) that review cannot intercept the irreversible action. A coherent tail constraint is infeasible for every non-preventive control, so nothing substitutes for prevention. An irreducible catastrophic core appears here for the first time. Chapter 2 is the pivot from model risk to systemic risk. Lifting the unit to a fleet of agents sharing a foundation model, the chapter shows that the shared model is a non-diversifiable common exposure whose expected-shortfall floor holds however large the fleet grows, a monoculture that no amount of redundancy dilutes. A percolation threshold governs contagion through the inter-agent dependency graph, and fleet architecture controls that threshold; segmentation and heterogeneity that keeps an exploit from transferring both lower the threshold, but only prevention or severing the common exposure moves the systemic floor itself. The chapter then lets agents respond to each other, opening two further channels. When an agent’s activation depends on the rest of the fleet, harm becomes a fixed point rather than a sum, and a social multiplier that grows with peer deference rescales the fleet average and the non-diversifiable floor; if that deference itself rises under stress, the fleet gains a common factor even without a shared shock. A compromised peer can also become a persuasion channel alongside the technical one, and segmenting the technical graph alone no longer caps the outbreak once this second channel is contagious on its own. Chapter 3 renders these systemic dynamics in continuous time as a marked, jump-diffusion, Hawkes-excited process. The static decomposition reappears as the rare-event limit of a compensator identity. The fleet results reappear as a common-L´evy-jump systemic floor and a Hawkes spectral-radius criticality for self-exciting cascades. We show that the robust (worst-case) stress problem coincides exactly with a time-consistent entropic risk measure, so robustness to misspecification and dynamic consistency are one object, with the prevention lever reappearing as the jump-measure truncation that makes the robust game finite at all. Chapter 4 turns to macroprudential control and its limits, modelling runtime guardrails and circuit-breakers as partially-observed stochastic control. The chapter gives an observability trichotomy for violation directions and a non-diversifiable detection floor that mirrors the monoculture result. The chapter also gives a runtime-impossibility corollary (of commit-exogeneity, Assumption 4.12), the dynamic form of the macroprudential thesis. Against an irreversible systemic event, the probability of eventually exiting safety depends only on the irreversible-core hazard rate and is identical across every runtime policy, so no amount of monitoring or intervention substitutes for the ex-ante, structural measures that lower that hazard rate itself. Chapter 5 makes the adversary a player. The chapter studies agentic-AI-augmented cyber events and shows that an unintentional event, a bad update or a poisoned dependency, reduces to the common shock of the earlier chapters when modeled as a fleet-wide, exogenously-timed trigger.

title: The Three-Month Sprint: How an African Scholar-Journalist Developed Three Original Frameworks in Ninety-One Days

detail.title: The Three-Month Sprint: How an African Scholar-Journalist Developed Three Original Frameworks in Ninety-One Days

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No relationship
declarations.funderStatement: Sundiata Post Media Ltd

contentType.other: A standalone special report of the Sundiata Post Intelligence Unit (SPIU), Abuja, Nigeria

detail.abstract:
Between 8 March and 7 June 2026—a span of ninety-one days—an African scholar-journalist working through an independent Nigerian newsroom developed three original analytical frameworks: the Insecurity Triad, an interpretive framework for organised insecurity in Nigeria and the Sahel; the Trinity of Sovereignty Decay (formerly Trinity of State Decay, TSD), a theoretical framework on sovereign decoupling and rival sovereignty; and the Decoupling Sovereignty Index (DSI), a twenty-seven-indicator quantitative instrument for measuring the severity of sovereign decoupling. This working paper is not a restatement of the substantive claims of these frameworks, each of which is documented in its own dedicated work. Rather, it is a documentary and reflective account of the conditions, sequence, and institutional logic through which three distinct intellectual constructs were developed within a newsroom rather than a university department.

The paper reconstructs the intellectual origins and day-by-day chronology of the Three-Month Sprint and examines what the sequence reveals about the location and institutional conditions of knowledge production. It argues that the Sprint constitutes a case—not a proof, but a documented instance—of media-based knowledge production operating as a parallel channel to academic knowledge production, with particular relevance to Global South contexts where university research infrastructure may be constrained relative to the scale and urgency of the problems requiring sustained analysis. The paper further examines the relationship between journalism, original conceptual development, institutional research capacity, scholarly dissemination, and emerging forms of algorithmic discoverability. It concludes with a research agenda for journalism studies, the sociology of knowledge, and scholarship on Global South intellectual production, while situating the Sprint as a documented case through which the boundaries between journalism, independent scholarship, and institutional knowledge production can be reconsidered.

It concludes with a research agenda for journalism studies, the sociology of knowledge, and scholarship on Global South intellectual production, while situating the Sprint's outputs within an expanding research and repository infrastructure through which work originating outside conventional academic institutions can become independently inspectable and citable.

title: Knowledge Management and Organizational Resilience in Crisis: A Systematic Review of Capacities, Mechanisms, and Consequences 2
affiliations: Islamic Revolution University, Imam Hossein University and Imam Hossein University

detail.title: Knowledge Management and Organizational Resilience in Crisis: A Systematic Review of Capacities, Mechanisms, and Consequences 2

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: Recent crises have demonstrated that organizational resilience depends not only on resources, technologies, and formal structures but also on organizations' capacity to mobilize knowledge under conditions of uncertainty and time pressure. This systematic review synthesizes fragmented evidence on how knowledge management (KM) contributes to organizational resilience across crisis stages and outcomes. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, peer-reviewed studies indexed up to December 31, 2025, were systematically identified, screened, and appraised, resulting in 52 eligible studies. Thematic synthesis identified five interdependent KM capacities: strategic and environmental awareness; absorptive and reconfigurative learning, including unlearning; social capital and relational coordination; organizational memory and institutional continuity; and adaptive responses and innovation. Four mechanisms explain how these capacities foster resilience: reducing ambiguity and accelerating decision-making, enabling collective action and resource mobilization, institutionalizing experience through recursive learning, and facilitating improvisation and innovation. The contribution of KM varies across resilience outcomes and crisis stages. Strategic awareness and organizational memory are particularly important for recovery, learning, and relational capacities that support adaptation, while unlearning and innovation become critical for transformation. The evidence also reveals non-linear effects: knowledge accumulation may generate inertia and rigidity, while uncertainty, transition costs, trust, organizational structure, and digital infrastructure condition KM effectiveness. Building on these findings, this review develops a processual and recursive framework that conceptualizes KM as an evolutionary meta-capability for configuring complementary knowledge capacities across crisis cycles. This perspective extends resilience research beyond static resource-based explanations and provides a foundation for the longitudinal and comparative testing of KM mechanisms and boundary conditions.

detail.abstract: Structural transition is changing the institutional parameters that give capability meaning across institutions, economies and societies. In Africa, technological transformation, artificial intelligence, demographic change, climate and energy transition, industrial restructuring, regional integration and changing relations between learning and work are unfolding within the same historical period. These are not independent pressures acting on otherwise constant systems. They interact and co-evolve, affecting both the capabilities societies and institutions require and the environments through which those capabilities acquire significance.

title: Machine Verification and the Institutions of Trust: Reputation, Certification, and Contract when Checking Becomes Cheap

detail.title: Machine Verification and the Institutions of Trust: Reputation, Certification, and Contract when Checking Becomes Cheap

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author holds commercial interests in automated verification of commercial energy billing.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical study and reports no research involving human participants or patients.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Many institutions of commerce exist because verification is expensive: brands bond unobservable quality, certifiers amortize the fixed cost of checking, and intermediaries are paid, in part, a verification wage. This paper asks what happens to those institutions when machine intelligence lowers the cost of two historically expensive tasks: establishing whether existing obligations were satisfied (conformity), and whether a better contractual arrangement exists (optimality). In a model where trading relationships choose among opacity, reputation bonds, third-party certification, and direct machine verification, five results follow. First, verification de-institutionalizes: amortization vanishes with construction costs, and because shared-certifier adoption is strategically complementary, certification markets can end by tipping rather than decay. Second, brands migrate rather than die: the bonding share of brand value compresses toward the cost of credibly attested verification while search, taste, and status shares persist. Third, optimality rents compress through repricing and exit: as individualized counterfactuals become cheap, the minimum mismatch worth acting on falls, incumbents reprice before customers switch, and compression stops at switching friction, not zero. Fourth, accusing gets cheap faster than proving innocence, expanding nuisance challenge unless rebuttal costs fall symmetrically or fee-shifting intervenes. Fifth, opacity relocates toward unverifiable attributes. An implementation in commercial energy contracting operationalizes both layers, with the verifier construction-cost series K(t) as a novel measured object.

title: Personalized Pricing Under Limited Capacity
affiliations: , Fudan University - School of Management, Fudan University - School of Management and Washington University in St. Louis - John M. Olin Business School

detail.title: Personalized Pricing Under Limited Capacity
detail.abstract: This paper examines the interaction between personalized pricing and capacity constraints in a two-period framework with forward-looking consumers. We introduce the valuation-identification precision parameter— the probability that a returning customer’s exact willingness-to-pay is correctly identified and subsequently applied in individualized pricing—as a measure of a firm’s capability under personalized pricing. Returning customers whose valuations are not successfully identified are offered a uniform price. Our analysis yields three main findings. First, compared with uniform pricing, a capacity-constrained firm under personalized pricing may deliberately leave some unidentified returning customers unserved in the second period. This rationing mechanism renders the effect of identification precision on initial prices capacity-dependent: higher precision increases initial prices under low capacity but reduces them under high capacity. Moreover, capacity expansion does not necessarily lower prices; beyond a non-binding threshold, the firm may abandon market clearing and raise initial prices. Second, the optimal capacity exhibits an N-shaped relationship with identification precision—rising at low and high precision levels but declining at intermediate levels. Third, higher identification precision may reduce consumer surplus under low capacity, yet enhance it when capacity is abundant. In certain scenarios, capacity restraint yields simultaneous gains for the firm, consumers, and social welfare. These results offer capacity-contingent guidance for integrating personalized pricing strategies with operational scale decisions.

title: Spatially Resolved Rainfall-Aware Routing for Automated Vehicles Using Sparse Crash Evidence
affiliations: Ostfalia Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften and Ostfalia Hochschule für angewandte Wissenschaften

detail.title: Spatially Resolved Rainfall-Aware Routing for Automated Vehicles Using Sparse Crash Evidence
detail.abstract: Rainfall is a well-established route-safety hazard, yet most research estimates weather-related crash risk without translating it into operational decision support. This study develops an end-to-end framework linking rainfall-associated crash-odds estimation to spatially resolved rainfall-aware routing for automated vehicles (AVs). Rainfall associations were estimated using time-stratified case-crossover analyses of California AV crashes. A commensurate-prior model incorporated information from a larger conventional-vehicle crash sample. The posterior coefficient was combined with a monotone, sensor-informed rainfall-severity basis to construct a rainfall multiplier, which was propagated into scenario-specific route evaluation. Policies were calibrated independently and evaluated across 42,000 held-out origin-destination-storm combinations in Berlin against a frozen static risk-aware policy, a detour-matched static control, and a spatially uniform rainfall control without spatial rainfall variation.Under the selected modeled-risk–distance trade-off, spatially resolved rainfall-aware routing reduced scenario-conditioned modeled route risk by 5.41% and the rainfall-responsive modeled-risk component by 23.70%, while increasing portfolio distance by 5.06%. Scenario-conditioned modeled-risk reductions were largest under widespread, high-intensity rainfall, which also produced the largest detours. At comparable detour levels, the static control achieved greater scenario-conditioned modeled-risk reduction, whereas the spatially resolved policy achieved the greatest rainfall-responsive reduction. Posterior propagation yielded a median scenario-conditioned modeled-risk reduction of 5.57%, with a 95% interval of 3.92–8.27%. The findings support spatial rainfall information as a selective, uncertainty-aware extension of static risk-aware routing rather than a universally superior routing strategy.

title: Scaling Maturity: A Theoretical Framework for Self-financed Scaling in Tech Startups

detail.title: Scaling Maturity: A Theoretical Framework for Self-financed Scaling in Tech Startups

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author reports no personal or financial relationships with other people or organizations that have influenced, or could be perceived to have influenced, this study. This working paper was written independently as private research. It was not commissioned, funded, or reviewed by any company.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper is a theoretical framework and does not involve patients, human participants, or case-study subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces Scaling Maturity as a theoretical framework for understanding and achieving sustainable growth in self-financed tech startups. We define Scaling Maturity as the capability to repeatedly transform growth-induced pressure into precise structural adaptations that stabilize the system before further expansion. The framework consists of three interconnected components: (1) Scaling Maturity as a capability, (2) scaling readiness as an empirical state, and (3) a core sequence (Pressure → Clarity → Small Redesign → Stability → Scaling) as the operational process. Through this triangulation, we provide a complete theoretical foundation that distinguishes between growth (proportional expansion) and scaling (leverage-based expansion), offering a systematic approach to scaling that avoids the common pitfalls of premature expansion. The framework addresses a critical gap in entrepreneurship literature by providing a mechanism-based approach to scaling that is specifically tailored to the constraints of self-financed startups operating without external capital.

title: The Argentine Case: Crisis as the Material Revelation of the Law of Value

detail.title: The Argentine Case: Crisis as the Material Revelation of the Law of Value
detail.abstract: This article argues that the Argentine economic crisis, like the Cuban one, has its ultimate cause in the systematic distortion of the relationship between value and commodity prices. While Cuba has repressed value through planned prices below production costs, Argentina has distorted it by excess through indexation to the dollar as an artificial reference. Unlike conventional approaches-which attribute the Argentine crisis to "management errors" or "populist legacy"-this study demonstrates that it is a structural crisis of capitalism, generated by a mediation that prevents prices from returning to their value. We provide a regressive-structural method to observe the causal action of value over time, showing that it manifests in three moments before market mechanisms operate: the contraction of consumption (hunger), the search for value abroad (cross-border shopping), and the destruction of national industry. We conclude that palliatives-massive imports in Argentina, the ration book in Cuba-do not resolve the distortion, and that the only morally and materially superior alternative is the transformation of productive forces, not at the expense of living labor (wages), but through the development of dead labor (technology and automation).

title: Sindh's Socio-Economic Crisis: The Exploitative Hegemony of Wadera Shahi and a Case for Historical Facts
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Sindh's Socio-Economic Crisis: The Exploitative Hegemony of Wadera Shahi and a Case for Historical Facts
detail.abstract: Acknowledging the contributions of various nations, communities, and immigrant groups to the history, construction, and development of any region or society is a realistic perspective. However, alongside this recognition, an uncompromising and fair analysis of the local population's historical and economic background, their contribution to the economy, and the internal exploitative system is equally imperative. Historical & Educational Background: The Foundational Role of Minority Communities Prior to the creation of Pakistan, the primary credit for establishing the fundamental infrastructure in modern education, medicine, and social services in Karachi and broader Sindh lies with Sindhi Hindus, Parsis, the British administration, and Christian missionaries. During British rule, the Hindu Rajput and Lohana communities of Sindh rapidly embraced modern education, emerging prominently in administrative affairs, civil services, and commerce. While the local feudal and Wadera (landlord) class deliberately kept the rural population alienated from education, these minority communities utilized their personal capital and philanthropic vision to establish institutions that remain integral to Sindh's proud heritage.

title: A Simulation Model for Predicting Tramp Shipping Supply
affiliations: Roskilde University, Roskilde University, , Roskilde University and

detail.title: A Simulation Model for Predicting Tramp Shipping Supply

publicationDetails.detailsText: NHH Dept. of Business and Management Science Discussion Paper No. 2026/10
publicationDetails.journalName: Norwegian School of Economics, Department of Business & Management Science Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Tramp shipping is a key part of the maritime industry which operates mainly in the spot market relying on voyage-by-voyage contracting, which forces them to reposition frequently in search of favourable cargoes. Market dynamics therefore emerge from how regional cargo demand aligns with the shifting distribution of available vessels. Forming multi-month forecasts of this evolving relationship between demand and supply is essential for market participants seeking to respond to rapidly changing market conditions. The supply side of the relationship remains relatively unexplored, particularly addressing vessels reposition and evolvement of regional availability over time. Bridging this gap, this paper introduces a simulation-based framework that models behaviour at the individual-vessel level and generates forward-looking forecasts of regional tramp-shipping supply over a 90-day horizon. The regional tramp shipping vessel supply prediction is presented through a mathematical formulation and an agent-based framework in which each vessel acts as an autonomous agent responding to market conditions is developed. To this end Neural network-based stochastic estimators of vessel behaviour are produced from historical data and used to simulate vessel-level decisions, yielding coherent forecasts of regional vessel supply. The framework is evaluated on the clean petroleum products market using datasets spanning the period 2020-01-01 to 2024-06-30. The results are compared with a regression benchmark relying on macroeconomic variables, and the developed framework show to achieve higher supply prediction accuracy in 23 of 24 region-(vessel-segment) combinations, reducing average mean absolute percentage error from 13.01% to 4.79%.

title: US vs. China, Round Two: China's Shifting AI and Supply Chain Strategy and Korea's Response

detail.title: US vs. China, Round Two: China's Shifting AI and Supply Chain Strategy and Korea's Response

publicationDetails.detailsText: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade Research Paper No. 26/MER/07/01
publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
US-China competition has moved past its first round, a contest of trade and technology pressure fought over tariffs and core technologies, and is evolving into a race to capture the global AI ecosystem of the physical AI era and to set the standards for industrial architecture. China is pursuing three shifts in its AI and supply chain strategy. First, as the effectiveness of US export controls erodes, it is building both leverage over demand markets and a semiconductor ecosystem of its own. Second, as the only country that covers every branch of industry in the UN industrial classification, it is applying AI to upgrade even its traditional manufacturing sector, turning manufacturing as a whole into a strategic asset. Third, it is using physical AI to extend its manufacturing and process-based standards worldwide. 

The second round of this competition calls for a Korean response that goes beyond a defensive diversification of supply chains. That response should center on three lines of action: building a K-manufacturing architecture that vertically integrates chokepoint assets with a manufacturing large language model (LLM) trained on the judgment data of demanding production processes; upgrading the K-materials industry by applying AI to traditional flagship industries; and pursuing the architectural assetization of K-manufacturing by binding Korea's separate strengths in technology, production capacity, standards, and shop-floor data into a single asset system. The indispensable assets developed in this way should in turn support deeper strategic partnerships, ones in which Korea participates in the technology ecosystems of major economies as a co-designer rather than a component supplier.

This paper was translated from the original Korean using the Claude Opus 5 large language

title: The Golden Era’s Guide To Entrepreneurship
